messages:
maria_ops: Heads up — seeing spikes on local NVMe across ephemeral-pool-a for the last 2 hours. Multiple model-serving pods stalled and restarted with I/O errors. Example from node logs:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:01Z] nvme0n1: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, status: 0x2
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] EXT4-fs error (device nvme0n1p1): ext4_wait_block_bitmap: blocked on I/O
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] ovs-vswitchd: delayed dp recirc due to high disk latency
```

maria_ops: Also saw ephemeral-cleaner container crash with "rm: cannot remove '/local/models/abc': Input/output error" :grimacing:

raj_infra: Which instance type / GPU fleet? Any pattern by job type?

maria_ops: Mostly p4d-style hosts (our dedicated GPU pool), ~12 nodes affected. Correlates with nightly large-batch eval jobs that stage many model checkpoints to local disk.

ben_sre: I pulled one crashed node: kubelet shows oom/killed for cleanup-agent, but dmesg shows NVMe I/O timeouts. Ran a quick fio: `fio --name=randrw --rw=randrw --bs=4k --size=2G --numjobs=8 --iodepth=32` and saw 99th pct latencies > 200ms and massive queue depth.

ben_sre: Pod log snippet: "ephemeral-cleaner: unlink /local/models/old: Input/output error" then container OOMKilled when it retried deleting lots of small files.

kai_storage: This looks like write-amplification / wear hotspot. Staging many small checkpoint files can thrash NVMe FTL. Two immediate mitigations: 1) throttle staging job IO (reduce iodepth / parallel writers), 2) move checkpoint staging to remote storage (tmpfs->S3) for batch jobs.

raj_infra: Agreed. Short term I can add a QoS/cgroup io.weight for the batch job containers to cap burst IO. If we need kernel-level controls we can use cgroup v2 io.max to limit bytes/sec for that slice. I'll prepare a safe rollout.

maria_ops: I'm going to cordon and drain the worst nodes now, and reschedule affected pods to other pools. Command I'll run: `kubectl cordon gpu-ephemeral-07 && kubectl drain gpu-ephemeral-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

deploy-bot: [auto] Sentry report created: ephemeral-cleaner v2.3 crash "Input/output error" — ticket INF-3245.

tess_mlinfra: Longer-term we should: add per-node NVMe SMART and wear-level metrics to Redwood Console, decrease default concurrency for checkpointing in our eval harness, and add an option to stream checkpoints directly to object store instead of local disk when running large-scale evals.

ben_sre: Also propose adding an alert: node disk avg await > 5ms for 1m and >70% util sustained -> auto-cordon. That avoids cascading restarts.

kai_storage: I'll run a non-destructive nvme health check on a drained node and talk to the cloud provider about possible firmware patches — there have been drive-level fixes for IO stalls in recent nvme firmware. If drives are degraded we'll rotate hosts.

maria_ops: Thanks — action items: raj to push cgroup io limits for batch jobs (ASAP), kai to run nvme health + firmware check (today), tess to add dashboard item + change default checkpointing concurrency (this sprint). I'll follow up on INF-3245 with logs and pod images. :thumbsup:

raj_infra: Starting canary change to batch-job helm chart to set io.weight=200 for staging containers, will monitor.

ben_sre: Copying notes to postmortem if we confirm firmware or workload cause. For now cordoned 3 nodes, rescheduled ~18 pods, alerting tuned.

maria_ops: Thanks team — keeping this thread for updates.
